title: Universal Tool Registry — System Overview
description: The registry is real, working software: 13 tools cataloged and queryable by name, capability, and free text.
body: The Universal Tool Registry is the first of the five foundational systems in Manon's Signature engineering AI. It is a genuine Node.js program, not a description of one: every tool is a structured record carrying capabilities, interfaces, dependencies, supported platforms, and execution status. The demonstration runs the registry's own summary command against its seeded catalog — 13 tools, broken down by verification status — and the output shown is the program's real output, captured at build time. Nine entries come from his 2026-10-21 "100 essential software developer tools" paste and are honestly marked proposed, because a pasted capability list is not running software. Two are host tools verified on this machine, and two are the sibling systems built in this same project, marked tested.

title: Registry Data Schema — What a Tool Record Carries
t: Registry Data Schema — What a Tool Record Carries
description: Every tool record carries name, description, capabilities, interfaces, dependencies, platforms, execution status, and source.
body: A tool record is a fixed-shape object. Name is required and unique; capabilities, interfaces, dependencies, and platforms are string arrays; execution_status must be one of proposed, generated, executable, tested, independently-verified, or verified-on-this-host; source records where the entry came from. The demonstration feeds the validator an empty name and prints the real rejection, proving the schema is enforced rather than decorative.

title: Adding a Tool — the add API
t: Adding a Tool — the add API
description: New tools enter through add(), which validates the schema and rejects duplicates by name.
body: The add path is the registry's only write door, and it validates before it stores. The demonstration adds a "Demo Linter" with a linting capability and proposed status; the program echoes back the stored record, including its defaults. A second add with the same name would be refused — that rejection is demonstrated in the limits record.

demo.program: node universal-tool-registry.js add {"name":"Demo Linter","description":"Example linter added via the API.","capabilities":["linting","static analysis"],"execution_status":"proposed","source":"demo"}

title: Query by Capability — findByCapability
description: Ask what a tool can do — "code generation" — and the registry returns every tool advertising it.
body: Capability search is substring-based and case-insensitive, so "code generation" matches the JAH Generator Runtime Engine. This is the query the master coordinator uses when an objective needs a capability: it asks the registry what exists before it asks anything to build. The demonstration shows the real match set.

title: Execution-Status Tracking — Tools Graduate as They Are Proven
t: Execution-Status Tracking — Tools Graduate as They Are Proven
description: setStatus moves a tool along proposed → generated → executable → tested → independently-verified.
body: A registry that cannot record proof is a phone book. The status ladder is enforced: only the six canonical values are accepted, and unknown values are rejected. The demonstration promotes the Linter from proposed to tested inside a live registry instance and prints the updated record — the same promotion path the other four systems earned by actually passing their demonstrations.

title: Persistence — Save the Registry, Load It Back
t: Persistence — Save the Registry, Load It Back
description: The catalog survives restarts: save() writes JSON, load() restores it with validation.
body: In-memory is fast but forgetful. The registry serializes its tool array to a JSON file and reloads it through the same add() validation, so a corrupt or duplicate entry in the file is caught at load time rather than silently stored. The demonstration performs a full round trip — save 13 tools, load into a fresh registry, count — and prints the real counts.

title: Limits and Honest Boundaries
description: The registry catalogs tools; it does not execute them, reach the network, or verify claims it cannot test.
body: Plain limits. The registry never runs a tool's code — execution status is a recorded claim, and only "verified-on-this-host" and "tested" were earned by running something here. It stores in memory (or one JSON file), so it is not a multi-user database. Duplicate names are rejected, unknown statuses are rejected, and malformed records are rejected — the demonstration shows the duplicate-name rejection on the real code path.

title: Integration — Feeding the Master Coordinator
description: The master coordinator calls findByCapability() per objective keyword; this record proves that contract.
body: Integration is a function call, not a diagram. The demonstration replicates exactly what the master coordinator does: extract keywords from an objective, query the registry per keyword, and collect the candidate tools with their statuses. The output is the real handoff payload the master consumes in its stage-2 delegation.
